html-a09-svg.q: Your 24x24 icon looks blurry when the design team scales it to 96x96 in the hero section. Which change fixes it for every size at once?
options: Export the icon as a 96x96 PNG and swap files per breakpoint
Rebuild the icon as SVG with a viewBox, and let width/height or CSS set the rendered size
Add image-rendering: crisp-edges to the existing PNG
Double the PNG's width and height attributes in the HTML
html-a09-svg.why: A vector with a viewBox is re-rendered from geometry at any output size, so one asset stays sharp everywhere; raster tricks only shuffle the blur around.

html-a09-svg.q: You inline an informational SVG chart legend. What is the correct way to make it accessible to screen readers?
options: Add a <title> element as the svg's first child and role="img" on the svg
Add alt="chart legend" to the svg element
Wrap the svg in a <figure> — that alone announces it
Set aria-hidden="true" so the reader skips the raw shapes
html-a09-svg.why: Inline SVG has no alt attribute; the accessible-name mechanism is a first-child <title> (plus role="img" so the drawing is treated as one image). aria-hidden is for decorative graphics only.

html-a09-svg.q: A polyline sparkline renders as a solid black blob instead of a thin line. What went wrong?
options: polyline requires closePath() before rendering
The points attribute must use semicolons between pairs
fill defaults to black and stroke defaults to none — you need fill="none" and a stroke color
polyline only works inside a <path> element
html-a09-svg.why: Shapes fill black by default and have no stroke; an open trace must explicitly set fill="none" and give the outline a stroke color.

html-a10-canvas.q: A canvas styled with CSS to 600x300 shows blurry, stretched drawings. Why?
options: The GPU compositor rounds coordinates on large canvases
The bitmap is still the default 300x150; CSS merely stretches it — set width/height attributes to 600 and 300
getContext("2d") was called before the styles loaded
fillRect antialiases unless lineWidth is set to 1
html-a10-canvas.why: Attribute width/height define the bitmap's real resolution; CSS only scales the rendered box, so a small bitmap gets stretched like a low-res photo.

html-a10-canvas.q: You call ctx.arc(100, 75, 50, 0, Math.PI * 2) but nothing appears on screen. What is missing?
options: A stroke() or fill() call — path commands only define geometry
The angles must be given in degrees, not radians
arc() requires a preceding closePath()
The canvas must have tabindex to receive drawing commands
html-a10-canvas.why: arc, moveTo and lineTo build an invisible path; pixels change only when stroke() or fill() executes it.

html-a10-canvas.q: You must render a live scatter plot with 50,000 points updating each second, and separately a static 12-node architecture diagram with clickable nodes. Which technology split is right?
options: Canvas for both — it is always faster
SVG for both — it is always more maintainable
SVG for the scatter plot, canvas for the diagram
Canvas for the scatter plot, SVG for the diagram
html-a10-canvas.why: Tens of thousands of frequently redrawn points overwhelm the DOM, so canvas wins there; a small interactive diagram gets events, CSS and accessibility for free as SVG.

html-a11-template-slot.q: Your script appends tpl.content to the page directly. The first card appears, but every later attempt stamps nothing. Why?
options: Templates self-destruct after one use by specification
Inserting a DocumentFragment MOVES its children out, emptying the template — clone with tpl.content.cloneNode(true) instead
The template needs a refresh() call between stamps
document.querySelector locked the template after the first read
html-a11-template-slot.why: A fragment's nodes relocate on insertion, so appending the content itself drains the blueprint; deep-cloning preserves the original for every subsequent stamp.

html-a11-template-slot.q: A third-party widget must keep its internal styles safe from any host page's CSS (and vice versa). Which mechanism provides that isolation?
options: Wrapping the widget in a <template> element
Using only named slots for all content
Attaching a shadow root and rendering the widget's markup inside it
Prefixing every class name with the vendor's name
html-a11-template-slot.why: Shadow DOM is the boundary: outer selectors do not reach in and inner styles do not leak out. Templates are inert storage and prefixes are only a convention.

html-a11-template-slot.q: You register a component with customElements.define("card", CardElement) and nothing upgrades. What is wrong?
options: define() must be called before the class is declared
Custom element names require a hyphen — "team-card" works, "card" is rejected
The class must extend HTMLDivElement, not HTMLElement
Custom elements only upgrade inside a <template>
html-a11-template-slot.why: The hyphen is how the parser separates author-defined tags from current and future built-ins; hyphen-less names throw at registration.

html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.q: Your drop handler on a kanban column never fires, though dragstart works and the ghost image follows the cursor. What is the most likely cause?
options: The dragged card is missing an id attribute
The column's dragover handler does not call e.preventDefault(), so the browser keeps rejecting the drop
dataTransfer.setData used "text/plain" instead of "text/html"
drop events only fire on <form> elements
html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.why: Every element rejects drops by default; cancelling dragover's default action is the required opt-in, and skipping it silently suppresses drop.

html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.q: In dragstart you try dataTransfer.setData("element", cardNode) to pass the card itself. What is the correct approach?
options: Use setData("text/plain", cardNode.id) and re-find the element with getElementById in the drop handler
Serialize the node with cardNode.toString() first
Attach the node to e.dataTransfer.files instead
Pass the node through a global variable — dataTransfer is only for files
html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.why: dataTransfer carries strings only; the idiom is to transfer an identifier and resolve it back to the live element on drop.

html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.q: A store finder works on localhost but on the deployed http:// site the location button does nothing. What explains it?
options: Production servers must whitelist the Geolocation API in robots.txt
getCurrentPosition needs enableHighAccuracy in production
Geolocation requires a secure context — HTTPS in production (localhost is exempt for development)
The permission prompt only appears for domains with a favicon
html-a12-drag-drop-geolocation.why: Powerful APIs like geolocation are HTTPS-only; localhost counts as secure for development, which is exactly why the bug appears only after deployment.

html-a13-storage-workers-sse.q: A user's saved filters must survive browser restarts, but the currently-open report tab should reset per tab. Where does each belong?
options: Both in localStorage with different keys
Filters in localStorage, open-report state in sessionStorage
Filters in sessionStorage, open-report state in localStorage
Both in cookies so the server can restore them
html-a13-storage-workers-sse.why: localStorage persists across restarts and is shared by all tabs; sessionStorage is scoped to one tab and cleared when it closes — exactly the two lifetimes described.

html-a13-storage-workers-sse.q: After localStorage.setItem("cart", cartObject), reading the value back gives the string "[object Object]". What went wrong?
options: The cart exceeded the 5 MB quota and was truncated
setItem requires a third argument declaring the type
Storage stores strings only — the object was coerced; use JSON.stringify on write and JSON.parse on read
Objects must be stored in sessionStorage, not localStorage
html-a13-storage-workers-sse.why: Any non-string value is stringified by coercion, and objects coerce to "[object Object]"; the JSON round-trip is the standard fix.

html-a13-storage-workers-sse.q: A live sports-score page only ever receives updates from the server and must survive flaky hotel Wi-Fi with minimal code. Best transport?
options: A WebSocket connection with a hand-written reconnect loop
Server-Sent Events via EventSource — one-way push over HTTP with automatic reconnection
Polling fetch() every two seconds
A Web Worker that holds the connection open
html-a13-storage-workers-sse.why: The traffic is strictly server-to-client, which is SSE's exact use case — and EventSource reconnects by itself, the code WebSocket would make you write.

html-a14-style-guide.q: A page renders fine for you, but the client's CMS mangles it and the validator reports dozens of errors. The markup uses unquoted attributes like class=hero box. What is the root cause?
options: The CMS requires XHTML 1.0 doctype declarations
Unquoted values end at the first space — class=hero box is class="hero" plus a junk attribute box; browsers guess, stricter tools do not
class attributes may not contain two words
The validator is misconfigured; unquoted attributes are invalid HTML5
html-a14-style-guide.why: An unquoted value terminates at whitespace, silently splitting the intended value; forgiving browsers hide the bug that stricter parsers expose.

html-a14-style-guide.q: During a code review you find <center><font color="red">Special offer</font></center>. What is the correct modernization?
options:
Replace with
Special offer
Keep it — browsers still render both elements
Replace with a semantic element carrying a class, and move centering and color into a stylesheet rule
Replace <font> with <big> since font sizing was the issue
html-a14-style-guide.why: The fix is separation of concerns: structure in HTML (a heading or paragraph with a class), presentation in CSS. align and inline styles just relocate the same anti-pattern.

html-a14-style-guide.q: Accented characters on a deployed page display as strange symbol pairs, though everything looked right locally. Which missing line is the prime suspect?
options: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width">
<meta charset="UTF-8"> early in the head
<html lang="en"> on the root element
<!DOCTYPE html> on line one
html-a14-style-guide.why: Without a declared encoding the browser guesses, and a wrong guess turns multi-byte UTF-8 characters into mojibake; the charset meta pins the decoding.

html-a15-debugging-validation.q: Your CSS rule 'table > tr' matches nothing, though the source clearly shows tr elements directly inside the table. What happened?
options: tr elements cannot be styled directly
The parser inserted a tbody between table and tr during repair — the DOM differs from your source
The rule needs !important to beat browser defaults
Tables must have an id before child selectors work
html-a15-debugging-validation.why: Browsers auto-insert tbody while parsing tables, so selectors run against a repaired tree; 'table tr' or 'tbody > tr' matches the reality.

html-a15-debugging-validation.q: The W3C validator returns 52 errors on your page. What is the professional next step?
options: Fix all 52 from the bottom up so line numbers stay valid
Ignore it — the page renders correctly in Chrome
Fix only the first one or two errors, then re-validate — early errors cascade into phantom ones
Switch the validator to warning-only mode
html-a15-debugging-validation.why: A single early malformation (an unclosed quote or tag) generates dozens of downstream messages; fixing top-down and re-checking collapses the list fast.

html-a15-debugging-validation.q: An element sits inside a different parent in the DevTools Elements panel than in view-source. What does that tell you?
options: DevTools renders a cached copy of the page
The server sent different HTML to DevTools
The parser repaired a markup error somewhere above it and adopted the element elsewhere — the difference is your bug report
The element has position: absolute in CSS
html-a15-debugging-validation.why: View-source shows the bytes you wrote; the Elements panel shows the repaired tree. A parent mismatch is the signature of a parser fix, usually caused by an unclosed or misplaced tag earlier in the source.

html-a16-project-full-site.q: Shared in a chat app, your landing page unfurls as a bare URL although you added <meta name="og:title" ...>. What is wrong?
options: og tags must appear in the body, not the head
Open Graph requires the property attribute — property="og:title", not name
The page also needs a <link rel="social"> element
Chat apps only unfurl pages with an RSS feed
html-a16-project-full-site.why: Open Graph is read from meta elements with property="og:*"; the name attribute variant is silently ignored by social crawlers.

html-a16-project-full-site.q: A keyboard user visiting your landing page must press Tab eleven times before reaching the hero content. What is the standard structural fix?
options: Reduce the navigation to fewer links
Add tabindex="-1" to every nav link
Move the nav element below main in the source
Make the first focusable element a skip link — an anchor targeting main's id
html-a16-project-full-site.why: A skip link (<a href="#main">) lets keyboard and screen-reader users bypass repeated navigation in one action; it is the expected first tab stop on professional sites.

html-a16-project-full-site.q: In the features section you must present two product models rated against six features. Which markup is correct?
options: A table with a caption and th cells using scope="col" and scope="row"
A CSS grid of divs — tables are deprecated for layout
Nested ul lists, one per model
A dl with each feature as dt and both ratings in one dd
html-a16-project-full-site.why: This is genuinely two-dimensional data — each value means something only at the intersection of a feature row and a model column — which is exactly what table, caption and scoped headers express. The deprecation applies to tables for page layout, not for data.
